title: Micro-CT Imaging of Iodine-Stained Rat Stomach
author: Deborah Jaffey
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.95ih84e
materials: Weigh rats to determine drug dose
Return the stomach to iodine solution.

steps.title: Diet Training
steps.instruction: Accustom 4 rats (within preferred weight distribution) to Dietgel ClearH20 (Catalog #72-06-5022) over several days.

substeps.instruction: Days 1-2: Supply regular rat chow and a half container of Dietgel in a dish at 11 AM.
Following days: Fast animals for 12 hours (7 PM to 7 AM), then feed Dietgel only at 7 AM for 30 minutes.
Provide regular meals after the 30-minute Dietgel window regardless of consumption.
Repeat 2 to 3 times until animals naturally consume Dietgel following overnight restriction.

steps.title: Dietgel Consumption and Selection
steps.instruction: Determine Dietgel intake and select animals for the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Fast rats for 12 hours overnight before the planned experiment.
Weigh empty bowls on a scale.
Place half a container of Dietgel ClearH20 (Catalog #72-06-5022) in bowls and reweigh to get filled bowl weights.
Place filled bowls in cages of fasted rats; allow them to eat for 30 minutes or until they stop.
Remove and reweigh bowls to determine amount eaten and record time as t0.
Select the 2-3 rats that consumed the most Dietgel and randomly assign them to perfusion times (intervals of at least 1 hour from t0).

steps.title: Anesthesia and Initial Preparation
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the rat and prepare for perfusion.

substeps.instruction: IP inject a cocktail of Ketamine (Patterson Veterinary Catalog #07-803-6637) and Xylazine (Akorn Inc Catalog #NDC: 59399-110-20) consisting of 10 mL of 100 mg/mL ketamine and 1 mL of 100 mg/mL xylazine (Total volume 11 mL). Use 2-3 mL/kg.
Open the thoracic cavity to expose the heart, inferior vena cava (IVC), and aorta.
Administer 0.5 mL Heparin (Henry Schein Animal Health Catalog #049130) into the right or left ventricle using a 26G needle.

steps.title: Perfusion Process
steps.instruction: Perform systemic perfusion with saline and paraformaldehyde.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a Masterflex peristalsis pump with appropriate tubing.
Start pump with 250 mL of 40 °C saline at 25 mL/min.
Thread a blunt 18G perfusion needle through the left ventricle apex into the aorta, ensuring it does not poke through to the right atrium/ventricle and does not go too far up the aorta.
Cut the right atrium and IVC to drain blood; clamp the needle with a hemostat if needed to prevent backflow.
Verify liver clearing (should be tan color after ~45 seconds); adjust needle if necessary.
Switch to 500 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.01M PBS at 25 mL/min after the initial 250 mL saline.

steps.title: Stomach Cannulation during Perfusion
steps.instruction: Insert tubes into the stomach and duodenum during the perfusion process to maintain patency.

substeps.instruction: Thread one feeding tube (5 Fr or 8 Fr) through the esophagus, stopping at the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) to avoid stretching the stomach.
Cut a small hole in the duodenum 2-3 cm from the pylorus.
Thread a 5 Fr feeding tube through the hole into the pylorus.
Cover exposed areas with Kimwipes and spray frequently with saline to keep moist.

steps.title: Stomach Extraction and Fixation
steps.instruction: Remove and fix the stomach tissue.

substeps.instruction: Remove all needles, tubes, and clamps; dissect out the stomach, leaving generous lengths of esophagus and duodenum.
Place the stomach in a glass jar with ~100 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde and store at 4 °C for approximately 24 hours.
Create a stock solution of I2/KI by adding 10 g of I2 and 20 g of KI to 1 L of ultrapure water; stir for at least one hour until dissolved.
Prepare a 0.1% I2 + 0.2% KI solution by mixing 100 mL of stock solution with 900 mL of ultrapure water.

steps.title: Stomach Flushing and Staining
steps.instruction: Clear the stomach of contents and stain with iodine.

substeps.instruction: Flush the stomach by holding it under saline and gently massaging to push food out through the pylorus; repeat until contents are removed.
Place the stomach in a glass jar containing the 0.1% I2 / 0.2% KI solution and place on a shaker table.
Squeeze out air if the stomach floats, flip stomachs every few hours, and replace solution as it loses tint.
Allow the stomach to absorb iodine for 24 hours.

steps.title: Gelatin Support Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare a gelatin solution to stabilize the stomach during scanning.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 4% to 5% (40 g/L to 50 g/L) type B gelatin solution in ultrapure water.

steps.title: Stomach Inflation and Stabilization
steps.instruction: Inflate the stomach with PBS to ensure repeatable dimensions.

substeps.instruction: Remove stomach from iodine solution and rinse in PBS.
Tie off the esophagus with a cotton thread bow, leaving at least 1 cm between the LES and the bow.
Attach a 5 Fr feeding tube to a 10 or 20 mL syringe filled with PBS; thread the tube through the duodenum and pylorus into the stomach.
Hold the duodenum skyward and slowly plunge the syringe to inflate the stomach until bubbles stop emerging.
Slowly remove the tube while plunging until the distal end is at the junction of the index finger and thumb at the open end of the duodenum.
Clamp the duodenum directly below the hold point with hemostats (do not clamp the tube).
Tie a bow 2-3 mm proximal to the clamp and remove the clamp.

steps.title: Micro-CT Scanning
steps.instruction: Image the stomach using the Quantum GX2 system.

substeps.instruction: Warm up the scanner (ideally 90 kV voltage and 88 µA current).
Under a ventilated hood, rinse the stomach with 10X PBS or saline.
Partially fill a 4 oz. PP container 3/4 with gelatin; place the stomach ventral side up, esophagus facing the back, and pylorus facing left, ensuring it is flat and completely submerged.
Place the container on the bore between the beam and detector.
Use Live Mode to adjust position and minimize the field of view (FOV) to capture the entire stomach (typically 45 mm, sometimes 60 mm or 72 mm).
Set parameters to High Resolution with at least a 14-minute scan time and start the scan.

steps.title: Post-Scan Processing
steps.instruction: Clean and preserve the samples after imaging.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the stomach to a PP container filled with saline/PBS and rinse off all gelatin.
Remove tie-off threads and return stomachs to 4% PF stored at 4 °C.
